clue.text: Acted like a vandal and was dismissed

definitions.meaning: to plunder or ransack a town, as the Vandals did Rome
was fired from a job

explanation.surface: Someone smashed things up at work and lost their job for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both looted (a city) and fired (an employee): two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Press men in China

definitions.meaning: to press-gang men, kidnap them into service at sea
the great port city of China

explanation.surface: Journalists working in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press men' suggests journalists, but it is a verb phrase: force men into service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese port gave its name to the practice of drugging or kidnapping sailors for a voyage.

clue.text: Gets up, but it involves a scramble

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or complicate, so the word that follows is jumbled

explanation.surface: Climbing a rock face means scrambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scramble' reads as a description of climbing, which suits the definition, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamber is to climb awkwardly using hands and feet, so it means gets up.

clue.text: Around midday set out the food

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the middle piece
set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in another order

parts.note: the middle letter of the word day is A

explanation.surface: Arrange a lunch at noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into ETS, and 'Around' puts that round A, the middle of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food or a meal.

clue.text: Nuts are found in them, and bolts

definitions.meaning: coal buckets hold nuts, small lumps of coal
bolts as a verb, runs off hurriedly

explanation.surface: A hardware joke about nuts and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts here are lumps of coal kept in a coal bucket, not hardware; 'bolts' is a verb meaning dashes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal buckets hold coal nuts, and to scurry away is to bolt: a noun plural and a verb.

clue.text: Bringing into force

parts.note: read as enlisting people into the armed forces rather than enacting a law

explanation.surface: A law being put into effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory military service means drafting citizens into the armed forces.

clue.text: Egotistical dedication for a book

definitions.meaning: a dedication reading '...', addressed to oneself
a large volume

explanation.surface: An author dedicates a book to themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large heavy volume, and split in two the word is a self-addressed inscription.

clue.text: Forms with no head girls

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: forms are school classes

explanation.surface: Schoolrooms without a headmistress, full of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasses are girls or young women, mainly in Scottish and Northern English usage.

clue.text: Last of the late-comers gets rot ten seat

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to addle is to go rotten, as an egg does

explanation.surface: The final latecomer gets the worst seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot ten' is the newspaper scan's split of 'rotten'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a rider's seat.

clue.text: Stays will alter a waist

indicators.note: altering the letters of the phrase rearranges them into a new word

explanation.surface: A corset will change the shape of a woman's middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a noun (corsets), which fits the waist picture, but it is the verb: remains waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay for something is to wait for it, so stays means is waiting for.

clue.text: Girl thought to be like Queen Victoria

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
mused means pondered or thought

explanation.surface: A young woman's thinking is compared to that of an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with the line 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous royal remark attributed to Victoria expresses displeasure, so her reputed mood was one of disapproval.

clue.text: Unreliable combination of opposites

definitions.meaning: to play this way is to behave irresponsibly
fixed and slack, two words of opposite sense joined

explanation.surface: A pair of contradictory qualities makes someone untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing this way means acting irresponsibly; its two key words, firm and slack, are opposites.

clue.text: Note retreat of W.African tribe to desert

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the tribe's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Ibo are a people of Nigeria

explanation.surface: A message about a West African people withdrawing into the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a great desert of Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: A month in advance

definitions.meaning: the third month of the year
to walk forward in step, as troops do

explanation.surface: A calendar entry in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the third month and also a verb for proceeding in military step.

clue.text: Inventor of the telephone or part of it

definitions.meaning: Alexander Graham ...
the ringer of an old telephone

explanation.surface: A trivia question about who devised the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone, whose ringer was a small metal chime.

clue.text: Record membership

definitions.meaning: to enter in a register or roll
to sign up as a member

explanation.surface: Someone has the highest number of members ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record membership' reads as a noun phrase, the most members ever; it is two verb senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to register a name officially, and to join as a member.

clue.text: Open a fresh page

indicators.note: a fresh arrangement of the letters gives a new word

explanation.surface: Starting on a new sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape means wide open, as a mouth in astonishment.

clue.text: Family ties for the mother's boy

definitions.text: Family ties for the mother's boy

parts.words: Family ties for the mother's boy
parts.note: the cords of a kitchen pinafore, figuratively the hold a mother keeps on a dependent son

explanation.surface: A son too attached to his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A man tied to his mother's pinafore cords is one still controlled by her.

clue.text: Turn a wench into a winch

parts.note: to wind is to turn a handle
a lass is a girl or wench

explanation.surface: A magic trick turning a girl into a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a hand-cranked hoisting drum, a kind of lifting machine.

clue.text: See great changes in economy travel

indicators.note: changes to the letters put them in a new order

explanation.surface: Big changes are coming to cheap travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship.

clue.text: Indicate the spot for country meeting

parts.note: to point to something is to indicate it
a point is a particular spot or place

explanation.surface: Someone is directed to a precise location for a rural gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase horse race run across country, a British rural sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-country horse race for hunting people is held as a rural event, a meeting in racing language.

clue.text: Making jokes with no beginning, purely visual

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: jocular means joking

explanation.surface: Humour that relies only on sight gags.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye or sight.

clue.text: Beats making money!

definitions.meaning: hits repeatedly
British currency units

explanation.surface: A profitable business is unbeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hits hard repeatedly, and is also the plural of the British currency unit.

clue.text: Short cut taken when hunting

definitions.meaning: a close haircut
a short riding whip carried on the hunting field

explanation.surface: A rider takes a shortcut across country in the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A close haircut and a short whip for riders share the same word.

clue.text: A tax return to distribute

indicators.note: a return here is a turning back, so the word for the tax is written backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for passage

explanation.surface: Filing a tax return and paying out what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' wants to be a tax return, but it is the reversal signal for TOLL, giving LLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or apportion.

clue.text: Vain and averse to work

definitions.meaning: futile, without effect
lazy

explanation.surface: A conceited and lazy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' suggests conceited, but here it means pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means both groundless or futile and lazy.

clue.text: Poe's house-owner is heartless employer

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter, removed here

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote The Fall of the House of Usher

explanation.surface: A landlord in a Poe story is a cruel boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who uses or employs something.

clue.text: Famous ship is short of freight

indicators.note: short of its first letter, the word is trimmed at the front

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: A celebrated vessel has run low on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth, carrying the Argonauts.

clue.text: Cricketer yearns to be a spinner

parts.note: longs means yearns
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A fielder dreams of becoming a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler, but it is the child's spinning toy. A long stop is a fielding position directly behind the wicketkeeper in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The long stop is a fielding position, so the term names the fielder in it.

clue.text: A jolly girl for the Fleet

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman heads for the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is old naval slang for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great fleet of warships, as in the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Kept quiet

definitions.meaning: set aside, booked, as a table may be
reticent, undemonstrative

explanation.surface: Someone kept silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means both booked or held back and reticent in manner.

clue.text: Mix us some pudding

indicators.note: mixing the letters stirs them into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to make dessert together.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dessert.
